# Reporting, MLflow, and the CLI

One experiment fits both main models and gets a Markdown model card. A standalone
HTML comparison dashboard and comparison table collect their diagnostics.
Reports and MLflow use **raw run predictions**, as in the
[prediction-scale convention](03-diagnostics.qmd#prediction-scales-used-in-this-book).

This optional operations recipe refits its own candidates. It creates every
report it logs; no workbook or fitted model from another chapter is required.
For a brief handoff, generate the card and comparison below and stop there.

{{< include _shared.qmd >}}

```{python}
import yaml

from azoic.mlops import log_run

portfolio = load_portfolio()
experiment_config = make_experiment_config(str(PORTFOLIO_PATH))
main_run = run_experiment(experiment_config, df=portfolio)
runs = [main_run]
metrics = comparison_table(runs)
```

```{python}
card_path = ARTIFACT_DIR / "model_card.md"
dashboard_path = ARTIFACT_DIR / "comparison_dashboard.html"

card_path.write_text(model_card(main_run), encoding="utf-8")
dashboard_path.write_text(comparison_dashboard(runs), encoding="utf-8")
```

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Verify report artifacts and display raw metrics"
assert metrics["model"].nunique() == 2
assert card_path.stat().st_size > 0
assert dashboard_path.stat().st_size > 0
print("Held-out comparison — raw rates")
display(metrics[["config", "model", "gini_test", "op_ratio_test", "deviance_test"]])
```

## Log runs to local MLflow

MLflow uses a local SQLite backend. Its artifact root is also placed under the
tutorial artifact directory. Each `log_run` call records the data fingerprint,
experiment and model parameters, all finite metrics, and the generated
artifacts. `setup_mlflow_tracking` is a tutorial helper in `_shared.qmd`;
`log_run` is the Azoic API. Only reports written above are attached, so an older
tariff workbook cannot be mistaken for an artifact of these new runs.

```{python}
import mlflow

tracking_uri, experiment_name = setup_mlflow_tracking()
tracking_database = (ARTIFACT_DIR / "mlflow.db").resolve()

artifacts = [card_path, dashboard_path]
mlflow_run_ids = [
    log_run(
        run,
        tracking_uri=tracking_uri,
        experiment_name=experiment_name,
        artifacts=artifacts,
    )
    for run in runs
]
```

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Verify logged metrics and artifacts"
client = mlflow.MlflowClient(tracking_uri=tracking_uri)
logged = [client.get_run(run_id) for run_id in mlflow_run_ids]

assert all(
    entry.data.params["experiment.data_fingerprint"] == main_run.data_fingerprint
    for entry in logged
)
assert all(
    f"{model_name}.gini_test" in entry.data.metrics
    for entry, run in zip(logged, runs, strict=True)
    for model_name in run.models
)
assert all(
    {Path(item.path).name for item in client.list_artifacts(run_id, path="artifacts")}
    == {Path(path).name for path in artifacts}
    for run_id in mlflow_run_ids
)

pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "run_id": mlflow_run_ids,
        "tracking_database": [str(tracking_database.relative_to(ROOT))] * len(mlflow_run_ids),
        "artifact_count": [len(artifacts)] * len(mlflow_run_ids),
    }
)
```

To inspect the run later, start the UI manually; rendering never starts a server:

```bash
uv run mlflow ui \
  --backend-store-uri sqlite:///examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/mlflow.db
```

## Drive the same workflow from the CLI

Save the experiment configuration as YAML, then run these commands from
the repository root. They write into the tutorial artifacts directory. The
render executes each command; only its result is shown below the command.

```{python}
config_yaml = ARTIFACT_DIR / "experiment_config.yaml"
config_yaml.write_text(
    yaml.safe_dump(experiment_config.model_dump(exclude_none=True)), encoding="utf-8"
)
assert config_yaml.stat().st_size > 0
print("Wrote experiment_config.yaml")
```

```bash
uv run azoic profile --data examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/portfolio_v3.parquet \
  --target claim_amount --exposure exposure --claim-count claim_count \
  --out examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/cli_screening.csv
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
import subprocess

screening_csv = ARTIFACT_DIR / "cli_screening.csv"
subprocess.run(
    [
        "uv", "run", "azoic", "profile",
        "--data", str(PORTFOLIO_PATH),
        "--target", "claim_amount",
        "--exposure", "exposure",
        "--claim-count", "claim_count",
        "--out", str(screening_csv),
    ],
    cwd=ROOT,
    check=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
assert screening_csv.stat().st_size > 0
print(pd.read_csv(screening_csv).to_string(index=False))
```

```bash
uv run azoic fit --config examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/experiment_config.yaml \
  --out examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/cli_model_card.md --quiet
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
cli_card = ARTIFACT_DIR / "cli_model_card.md"
subprocess.run(
    [
        "uv", "run", "azoic", "fit",
        "--config", str(config_yaml),
        "--out", str(cli_card),
        "--quiet",
    ],
    cwd=ROOT,
    check=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
assert cli_card.stat().st_size > 0
print(cli_card.read_text()[:600])
```

```bash
uv run azoic compare examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/experiment_config.yaml \
  --out examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/cli_comparison.csv
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
cli_comparison = ARTIFACT_DIR / "cli_comparison.csv"
subprocess.run(
    [
        "uv", "run", "azoic", "compare",
        str(config_yaml),
        "--out", str(cli_comparison),
    ],
    cwd=ROOT,
    check=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,

assert cli_comparison.stat().st_size > 0
print(pd.read_csv(cli_comparison).to_string(index=False))
```

Export the direct GLM with `--no-recalibrate` to preserve its raw prediction
scale. The training multiplier shown in scoring remains external to this workbook.

Without this flag, CLI export recalibrates on the stored training rows only,
keeping holdout claims out of the base. The earlier raw metrics still describe
the unadjusted estimator; evaluate the adjusted workbook separately on the holdout.

```bash
uv run azoic export-tariff --config examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/experiment_config.yaml \
  --model direct-tweedie-glm --no-recalibrate \
  --out examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/cli_glm_tariff.xlsx
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
cli_glm_tariff = ARTIFACT_DIR / "cli_glm_tariff.xlsx"
subprocess.run(
    [
        "uv", "run", "azoic", "export-tariff",
        "--config", str(config_yaml),
        "--model", "direct-tweedie-glm",
        "--no-recalibrate",
        "--out", str(cli_glm_tariff),
    ],
    cwd=ROOT,
    check=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
assert cli_glm_tariff.stat().st_size > 0
print("Direct GLM workbook — raw rates")
display(pd.read_excel(cli_glm_tariff, sheet_name="base_rate"))
```

### Optional: export a distilled GBM

As in [optional distillation](04-scoring-tariff.qmd#distil-the-gbm-into-an-executable-tariff),
create a separate structured teacher by copying the raw GBM's settings into the
GLM's preprocessing configuration. Save it before running the export command.
The CLI fits this teacher and its student on training rows, reserving the test
rows for fidelity evaluation.

```{python}
teacher_config = experiment_config.model_copy(update={
    "name": "fremtpl2-structured-teacher",
    "models": {
        "tweedie-lightgbm-tariff": experiment_config.models["tweedie-lightgbm"].model_copy(
            update={"preprocess": True}, deep=True,
        ),
    },
})
teacher_yaml = ARTIFACT_DIR / "teacher_config.yaml"
teacher_yaml.write_text(
    yaml.safe_dump(teacher_config.model_dump(exclude_none=True)), encoding="utf-8"
)
```

```bash
uv run azoic export-tariff --config examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/teacher_config.yaml \
  --model tweedie-lightgbm-tariff --distill --no-recalibrate \
  --out examples/_artifacts/fremtpl2/cli_distilled_tariff.xlsx
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
cli_distilled_tariff = ARTIFACT_DIR / "cli_distilled_tariff.xlsx"
subprocess.run(
    [
        "uv", "run", "azoic", "export-tariff",
        "--config", str(teacher_yaml),
        "--model", "tweedie-lightgbm-tariff",
        "--distill",
        "--no-recalibrate",
        "--out", str(cli_distilled_tariff),
    ],
    cwd=ROOT,
    check=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
assert cli_distilled_tariff.stat().st_size > 0
print("Distilled workbook — raw student rates")
display(pd.read_excel(cli_distilled_tariff, sheet_name="base_rate"))
```

## Operational boundaries

This book estimates the capped historical pure-premium layer. A deployable
price still needs decisions about large losses above the cap, claims development,
inflation, expenses, commission, profit, taxes, and business constraints.
The local MLflow store and workbook are review artifacts, not a deployed scoring
service or policy-system integration. Keep preprocessing, model, prediction
scale, and calibration factor together when handing work over.

Once these holdout results inform a change to features, tuning, factors, or
calibration, they become development evidence. Evaluate the revised decision on
fresh data or a reserved later period before claiming independent performance.
